**Chiumenti, Nicholas** and Andrew Dumont. 2026. [*Rural America's Philanhtropic Sector: Grantmaking and the Role of Philanthropy in Rural Communities.*](https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/usda-rd-rural-philanthropy-report-03122026.pdf) U.S. Department of Agriculture, Rural Development.

::: {style="padding-left: 2em;"}
<details>
  <summary>**Show Abstract:**</summary>
  > Philanthropic organizations provide a key source of flexible financial investment in the form of grantmaking in the United States. As a source of capital, grants can support feasibility studies and pilot programs, serve as matching funds for other resources, and act as loss-absorbing capital to mitigate risk and entice for-profit investment. Using data from the Internal Revenue Service, we develop a novel definition for philanthropic grantmaking organizations and examine geographic differences in access to philanthropic resources between urban and rural communities. We find that, while total grantmaking averaged $116 billion per year from 2014 to 2021, just 3.5% came from rural-based organizations. We also find that a larger share of public charities is based in rural communities and those public charities issue more in grants than private foundations when compared on a per-organization basis. This has important implications for practitioners seeking out philanthropic sources of investment for their communities.
</details>
